title: Build a customer interview analyzer
description: A system that reads your customer interview notes and keeps a running document of validated pain points, objections, and quotes.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

merge.title: Merge
merge.content: Combining changes from one branch into another. When you approve a pull request, the branch gets merged into main and those changes become part of the live version.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

granola.title: Granola
granola.content: An AI meeting notes app that listens to your calls and produces structured summaries, action items, and transcripts. Works in the background during Zoom, Google Meet, and in-person meetings. Useful as a source of raw material for AI workflows — feed transcripts into Claude for follow-ups or CRM updates.

children.text: [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/report/startup-failure-reasons-top/) found product-market fit problems behind 43% of the startup failures in its post-mortem study, the single most common cause named. This system reads your customer interview transcripts and notes and adds each new interview to a running document of validated pain points, objections, and direct quotes, grouped by theme, so a pattern across ten interviews shows up instead of getting buried in ten note files.

Solo and small founding teams are a growing share of new companies, and the gap between top performers and the median keeps widening, per [Stripe's research on solo founders](https://stripe.com/blog/top-solo-founder-traits), raising the cost of building the wrong thing before a build even starts.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) after each call, a saved [skill](#tooltip-skill), or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that watches your notes folder or meeting tool for a new transcript.
Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming where your interviews live, how many you run each month, and what you do with insights today.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that reads through my customer interview transcripts and notes and turns them into a running document of validated pain points, objections, and direct quotes I can reference before I build anything. Ask me questions, one at a time, about where my interview notes currently live, how many interviews I run in a typical month, whether I record calls or type notes live, and what I actually do with insights once I have them today. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview surfaces decisions you didn't know you needed to make, and the scope document becomes the brief for every build session after it.

items: Where interview recordings or notes land today, a call tool, a shared drive, or a notebook app.
Whether the tracker lives as a standing document the AI tool updates or a fresh output generated each time.
Who besides you needs to see a flagged contradiction between two interviews.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first in a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model). Then gather your meeting notes tool ([Granola](#tooltip-granola), Otter, Fireflies), your call recording or video tool (Zoom, Google Meet), and your notes and docs home ([Notion](#tooltip-notion), Google Docs). The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build and test the system on your newest interview file. The prompt below is one example; your scope document has the full version.

children.prompt:
Goal: Read the newest customer interview transcript or notes file and add its findings to my running pain-point tracker without duplicating what's already there.

Context: Interviews live in [folder or tool, e.g. a Google Drive folder, Granola, or a plain text export]. My tracker is a single document organized by theme, not by interview date. Each entry needs the pain point, the customer's own words, which interview it came from, and how many separate interviews have now raised it.

Rules:
- Never merge two different pains into one because they sound similar; flag them side by side instead and let me decide.
- Quote the customer directly rather than paraphrasing.
- If a pain point contradicts something an earlier interview said, flag the contradiction instead of picking a side.
- Output as a markdown table grouped by theme, sorted by how many interviews raised each one.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: sorting by theme instead of interview date is what makes a repeated pain visible, and flagging contradictions instead of resolving them keeps the call on you.

children.text: **Review.** Check against your scope. Direct quotes, correct groupings, contradictions flagged instead of resolved?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what went wrong ("these two aren't the same pain, split them") and fold each correction into the rules.

items: Add a running willingness-to-pay tag on any quote that mentions price.
Cross-reference new interviews against a standing list of hypotheses.
Auto-generate a one-page brief before each round summarizing what's still unvalidated.
Flag when the same three people keep raising a pain no one else mentions.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat turn the scope bar into pass/fail checks and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each interview update to my pain-point tracker, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, interview added, new pain points flagged, contradictions flagged, and corrections made. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns make a quietly-[merging](#tooltip-merge) tracker visible fast.

children.text: **Log** every run against the rubric. Note the date, which checks passed or failed, and what changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the rubric passes a few interviews straight, package the prompt and your corrected rules into a reusable AI skill, so every run starts from your defaults. A repeated failure earns its own skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s built-in skill-creator skill will interview you and write it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).

One durable failure mode. It will find a pattern in three data points if you ask it to. Require a minimum count before it calls a pain point validated, since the person who talks most in an interview isn't always the one who represents the market.

items: [CB Insights, Why Startups Fail](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/report/startup-failure-reasons-top/) — The product-market-fit failure-cause figure.
[Stripe, Solo founding is at an all-time high](https://stripe.com/blog/top-solo-founder-traits) — The solo-founder growth and performance-gap figure.
